schema_version.description: 1.1.0 adds a proposal's stage and parent_proposal_id, 1.2.0 its subject_ref; an older report carrying a newer field is refused. 1.3.0 adds scoped context/outcome reads and exact action execution without changing report fields. 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 change only the directive. 1.6.0 adds a proposal's row, rank, reach, amplifier_kind, features, serves and source_revision, and allows 40 proposals (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, The five rows). 1.7.0 adds a row proposal's because and brief, which a row then needs. 1.8.0 adds a row proposal's card, the full card a tap opens, which a row then needs. 1.9.0 lets a visibility or events row's email action (exact_payload) name Jonny's box (mailbox), and changes no report field. 1.10.0 adds web_analytics to the directive of an engine whose product has a Google Analytics site with the per-post breakdown, origin_candidates to the report of the engine whose meetings Control Center reads (Mindmake, features.meetings), and a row action's kind show_notes_ask (exact_payload), Jonny's show-notes note after a booking. 1.11.0 adds the prior-outreach read and changes no report field. 1.12.0 lets a version 2 email action (exact_payload) carry prior_mindmake, the Mindmake record its words were written from, and reads a send's version 2 action whole (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, Legibility drafts in his own box). 1.13.0 changes only the directive, the capabilities and the research desk. 1.14.0 adds a proposal's kind copy_open, the engagement task: a version 2 action (exact_payload) on channel engage with taps, each the exact words Krish copies and the public page he opens and posts on himself, behind the post wall, to no person, with no stage; it is refused on any older version. 1.15.0 changes only the directive (inspiration). 1.16.0 adds credits_spent, the prepaid credits a run spent against the directive's credits. 1.17.0 adds buffer_channels (the Buffer channel ids the engine posts on, and the ones it never touches), which a go-live of posts is approved against, and post_metrics, each post's numbers as Buffer shows them; an engagement tap on X, TikTok, Instagram or LinkedIn opens the exact post or profile. 1.18.0 adds found_routes, the booking addresses and form pages read out of answered research lookups, which Control Center records only when its own checks pass (Mindmake, features.found_routes). 1.19.0 adds circle, up to 50 public people for Krish's circle lane that Control Center matches to his network or files as cold contacts with no address, and mirror, the AI mirror's questions (Mindmake, features.circle, features.mirror). 1.20.0 adds priorities, obsessions, next_steps and instruction_acks, the engine's state on every place in Control Center and what it did with Krish's instruction, each refused before 1.20.0; send them only when the directive says features.engine_state. 1.21.0 adds inspiration_used, the inspiration cards Krish ticked that an asset you made used, which close his ticks (growth-makeyourmindup, features.inspiration_used); refused before 1.21.0. 1.22.0 adds answers_served, the venture requests (growth_answer_requests ids) the AI-answers specialist's research run asked (AEO-Engine only, features.answer_requests); refused before 1.22.0 and from any other engine.

exact_payload.description: The exact words to approve. On a row proposal (1.6.0), a version 2 action as JSON text: { version: 2, channel, recipient_contact_id, subject, body, form, mailbox, kind }, never an address. mailbox (1.9.0): krish, jonny or null; jonny on the visibility and events rows only. kind (1.10.0, optional): show_notes_ask or null, only on an email with mailbox jonny about a stage (subject_ref target:<id>): Jonny's one note to a host after his pitch was booked, asking for the brief link in the show notes, drafted once a stage only after booked_at is recorded (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, The show-notes note). An older report naming a kind is refused. 1.12.0: a send off the rows written as a version 2 email action may carry prior_mindmake { state, state_at, last_touch_at, by?, record_url? }, the Mindmake record its words were written from, on an email only (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, Legibility drafts in his own box); from 1.12.0 a malformed version 2 action on a send is refused here. asset_ref (no version, Mindmake only, once capabilities say features.asset_links): { url, title, purpose, expires_in_hours } on an email whose body carries url as a link of its own, url on mindmake.co or a Drive or Canva share, expires_in_hours 1 to 2160; Control Center mints one SendLinks link per recipient when it drafts and puts it where url stood, or holds the draft (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, An asset in an email). 1.14.0: the engagement task is { version: 2, channel: engage, kind: copy_open, body, taps }, with recipient_contact_id null and no subject, form or mailbox; taps is 1 to 25 of { label, text, url }, the words carrying no address or number and url a public https page with no login, chat, address or number in it.

stage.description: 1.1.0. An autonomous engine's plan (behind a wall, waiting on his yes), its go-live (send, post or spend) for his review, or a check-in (a strategy call naming its plan, with its progress in exact_payload).

parent_proposal_id.description: 1.1.0. The plan a go-live carries out. Required on a go-live.

subject_ref.description: 1.2.0. The person, stage or room the proposal is about, by the id Control Center gave the engine. His list keeps Control Center's own copy of the same subject instead.

row.description: 1.6.0: the row on Krish's home screen. A row proposal is a prepared send with stage null, a subject_ref, a rank, a source_revision and a version 2 action in exact_payload. Its title is the line on his phone, shown whole: at most 72 characters.

rank.description: 1.6.0: the engine's order within the row, 1 first.

value.description: A sourced number, or null. A number needs source_url and as_of, and its band must match it.

basis.description: What is counted: portfolio companies, members, learners a year, subscribers.

features.description: 1.6.0: what his reasons for a No filter on.

serves.description: 1.6.0: one of the directive's week_goals, word for word.

sha.description: The file's git blob SHA on the default branch when the words were written.

source_revision.description: 1.6.0: every file the words were written from. Control Center refuses the action once one has moved.

because.description: 1.7.0: the line under the title on his card, two lines of it: who they are and why them, in plain words. Required with row at 1.7.0, when the row's title is at most 56 characters.

brief.description: 1.7.0: the case he reads when he taps the card: who they are, how he knows them, why them, what a yes gets him, the reach and its basis. Required with row at 1.7.0.

who.description: Who they are and what their organisation does.

known.description: How he knows them: since when, through what, the emails each way and the last one. Never a claim the counts contradict.

why.description: Why them, and why now: whole sentences.

gain.description: What he gets if they say yes, tied to the week goal it serves: whole sentences, numbers only with their source.

angles.description: The angles to take, each a short name from the venture's own canon and a line tying it to this person.

sources.description: The public pages the facts came from. Never a profile or an address: a LinkedIn profile, mailto:, wa.me or tel: link is refused.

card.description: 1.8.0: the full card a tap opens: who they are, how he knows them, why them now, what he gets and the angles to take, with the pages the facts came from (Krish, 2026-10-27). Required with row at 1.8.0.

proposals.description: At most 10 before 1.6.0; 1.6.0 allows 40, a ranked queue for each of the five rows.

origin_candidates.description: 1.10.0, Mindmake only (features.meetings), optional: where the engine reads each of his recent meetings came from. The first candidate naming a path for the person he met is recorded at his good tap, once; any other path for them is kept as an assist (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, Held meetings and the good tap).

origin_ref.description: A stable id (contact:<id>, a proposal id) or a public https page, never an address.

withdrawn.description: 1.10.0, optional: your own pending proposals you take back, each with why. Each one Krish has not decided becomes expired and leaves his list; a decided one is left as it is. Never both proposed and withdrawn in one report.

suppression.description: Mindmake only, optional, at any version once capabilities say features.suppression: what the engine says to hide on his widget, by its own rule. It replaces every earlier list. Each list at most 500 entries and sorted as the engine sorts it (never and topics by code unit, the others by localeCompare), no entry twice; the whole at most 65536 bytes of JSON. Control Center checks the schema only and decides nothing from it yet (ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md, The suppression list and the taxonomy).

reach_floor.description: A candidate of this kind at this band or lower is hidden.

taxonomy.description: Mindmake only, optional, at any version once capabilities say features.suppression, sent once a run beside suppression: the engine's rows, kinds, bands, reasons, presses and row doctrine, names and whole numbers only, at most 2048 bytes of JSON. ask_for keys are its kinds and its values keys of row_for; row_for values are its rows. Control Center checks the schema only; its own lists still decide until the retirement step.

credits_spent.description: 1.16.0, optional (features.credits): prepaid credits this run spent, each against a pool in the directive's credits; it counts against your share in the next directive.

pool.description: A pool key from the directive's credits.

asset.description: What it made, in words; never an address.

buffer_channels.description: 1.17.0, optional: the Buffer channels this engine posts on, channel name to its one Buffer id, and the ids it never touches. A go-live of posts (growth-golive-manifest/1) is approved only when each post names exactly the id listed for its channel, never a denied id or one another engine lists.

post_metrics.description: 1.17.0, optional: each post's numbers as Buffer shows them. A number the channel does not show is null, never zero. Shown on Growth, Engines, where sends and saves per reach are marked as hypotheses.

proposal_id.description: The go-live it went out under, or null.

offdays.description: 1.17.0, optional, growth-makeyourmindup (W2.9): the week's off-day options as growth.py mix offdays writes them (growth-offdays/1). His list counts the ready ones from today on as Off-day posts: N ready.

found_routes.description: 1.18.0, optional, Mindmake only (features.found_routes): a booking address or form page read out of one of your own answered research lookups. Control Center records it on the stage (booking_contact_id with booking_source research, or an empty cfp_url) or on the guest only when its own checks pass, never over what is on record, and answers each route's outcome in the acceptance's found_routes.

subject_ref.description: target:<visibility_target id>, contact:<a guest's contact id> or guest:<guest record id>.

address.description: For kind email: the address exactly as the result shows it.

url.description: For kind form: the form page, on the same site as source_url.

source_url.description: The result in the lookup's evidence the route was read from.

request_id.description: The lookup it was read from: your own, answered, about this subject.

circle.description: 1.19.0, optional, Mindmake only (features.circle): public people for Krish's circle lane. Who, never how: any @ or a run of nine digits refuses the report. Control Center links the same full name at the same company, writes nothing on a name alone, files anyone else as a cold contact with no address, and answers each person's outcome and in_network in the acceptance's circle.

contact_id.description: Someone in his own network, a contact your context served, in place of source_urls.

show.description: The show you invite them onto, or null: Control Center files a guest record for it, which your invites then read.

mirror.description: 1.19.0, optional, Mindmake only (features.mirror): the questions an AI mirror asks Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini about one person, run on Krish's press. Each names the person as {name}; {company} is the only other fill.

priorities.description: 1.20.0, optional (directive features.engine_state): what the engine is chasing, most important first. One plain line each, with no address or phone number. Shown on every place in Control Center as reported, never inferred.

objective_key.description: The objective it serves, or null.

obsessions.description: 1.20.0, optional: Krish's own aims the engine will not let go of, quoted from its own docs as lines, never invented.

next_steps.description: 1.20.0, optional: what the engine does next, and who each step waits on.

instruction_acks.description: 1.20.0, optional, applied from live reports only: what the engine did with each instruction of Krish's it read (the directive's krish_instruction), by id only. A line says what it did, or why it is blocked and what would unblock it, and never quotes his words: engine repositories and their Actions logs are public. Forward only: received, then started or blocked, then done; nothing after done.

inspiration_used.description: 1.21.0, optional (directive features.inspiration_used), growth-makeyourmindup: the cards Krish ticked as a style to use (a suggestion in the directive's inspiration that carries an instruction) which an asset you made used, each with what you made, in words. A use reported after his tick closes it (Control Center's done-check sweep, inspiration_act). Never an address or a link.

answers_served.description: 1.22.0, optional, the AI-answers specialist only (directive features.answer_requests): the request_id of each venture request in the directive's answer_requests that this research run asked, its questions verbatim under that product's subject. Control Center marks each served; a replay changes nothing twice (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-12: AEO-Engine is the one AI-answers specialist every venture's engine calls).
